expected_symptom: A source variable is given a range of PIX virtual registers by -dxil-annotate-with-virtual-regs that then receives no !pix-alloca-reg-write at all, so a PIX consumer asking for that variable's members reads registers nothing ever wrote. Measured by check-2923.py, which prints "PIX-2923: DECLARED-BUT-UNWRITTEN" in that case. Controls: the unmodified PixStructAnnotation_SequentialFloatN shader, and the same repro with the parameter made inout, must NOT match (verified, at both -Od and -O1, on main and at every release).
godbolt_skip: Compiler Explorer can only run dxc. The symptom is in metadata written by the PIX passes (-dxil-dbg-value-to-dbg-declare, -dxil-annotate-with-virtual-regs), which live in dxcompiler.dll and are driven by dxopt, not by dxc; CE has no way to run them and no way to show ILDB metadata. repro.hlsl itself compiles cleanly (exit 0, no diagnostics) on every release tested, so a CE link would show a clean compile and nothing about the defect. The runnable repro is run-2923.cmd in this directory.
history: Regressed v1.6.2104 (2021-04-20, correct) -> v1.6.2106 (2021-07-01, wrong). Hand-run 22-build matrix (manual-case-history.txt), each release using its own dxc.exe and its own dxcompiler.dll for the PIX passes via "dxopt -external": no-match at v1.5.2003, v1.5.2010, v1.6.2104; match at v1.6.2106, v1.6.2112, v1.7.2207, v1.7.2212, v1.7.2212.1, v1.7.2308, v1.8.2403, v1.8.2403.1, v1.8.2403.2, v1.8.2405, v1.8.2407, v1.8.2502, v1.8.2505, v1.8.2505.1, v1.9.2602, v1.9.2602.24, v1.9.2607 and on main-debug. v1.4.1907 predates as_6_5 and is an invalid probe. The IR shape does not change across the transition: the six DW_OP_bit_piece shadow allocas for main's p exist at v1.6.2104 too, but there each carries a !pix-alloca-reg-write; from v1.6.2106 those writes stop. Cross-probe of {dxc 2104, dxc 2106} x {passes 2104, passes 2106} (manual-case-crossprobe.txt) shows the behaviour follows the pass DLL, not dxc, so the change is in lib/DxilPIXPasses. CAVEAT: v1.5.2003 (2020-03-25) is the release current when the issue was filed (2020-05-27) and it numbers this repro correctly, so the repro is a reconstruction from the issue text ("Not clear yet what set of structs are affected") and may not be the reporter's own instance. triage.py bisect cannot drive this repro because it is a 4-tool pipeline, not a dxc invocation.

summary: Still repros on main (1.9.0.5433, 13730886e): passing an amplification payload struct by value to a subroutine that calls DispatchMesh leaves main's own local mapped to six PIX virtual registers that are never written, with the six member writes numbered onto the inlined callee copy instead (both -Od and -O1); regressed in v1.6.2106 and numbered correctly in every earlier probeable release, so this agent-built repro may not be the reporter's 2020 instance.
title: Structs passed to subroutines (can) cause the numbering pass to get confused about offsets of members
